correctness_anchor: A loop repeats a body under a count or condition; a conditional chooses a branch on a given evaluation.
application_anchor: Contrast a three-repeat trace with one if statement using matched actions and ask students to predict a new trace.
reject_endorsement: Calling a single branch selection a loop or claiming loops never contain conditions.

correctness_anchor: Representations need explicit correspondence, not simultaneous decorative duplication.
application_anchor: Sequence manipulation, a simple animation and code; align the same state changes and check a student's translation between two forms.
reject_endorsement: Assuming adding modalities always improves learning.

correctness_anchor: Failure to learn from one animation cannot establish a child's cognitive limitation.
application_anchor: Check prior knowledge with a simple prediction, remove irrelevant motion, pause at state changes and compare explanations.
reject_endorsement: Diagnosing a fixed inability from one lesson.

correctness_anchor: Assignment updates a stored value; it is not mathematical equality.
application_anchor: Use labelled value cards and trace x=2 then x=x+1 to obtain 3; bridge from objects to code.
reject_endorsement: Treating x=x+1 as an inconsistent equation in a programming trace.

correctness_anchor: Low-skill templates can be drawn with boxes, arrows and numbered steps.
application_anchor: Supply a reusable text/table template and a filled example requiring no animation software.
reject_endorsement: Inventing a downloadable template or requiring specialist drawing tools.

correctness_anchor: Progression should preserve a concept while increasing one source of complexity at a time.
application_anchor: Show a concrete-to-trace-to-symbol progression with a readiness check and fallback.
reject_endorsement: Advancing by age alone without checking understanding.

correctness_anchor: Every analogy has a boundary; arrays add indexed elements rather than an unlimited single mailbox.
application_anchor: Map numbered compartments to indices and values, state where the analogy fails and verify a read/update example.
reject_endorsement: Promising an analogy that never breaks down.

correctness_anchor: Preferences and access needs do not imply fixed visual/auditory/kinesthetic learner types.
application_anchor: Offer linked representations chosen for content and accessibility, then check understanding rather than sorting students into permanent types.
reject_endorsement: Claiming matching teaching to a fixed learning-style label guarantees better learning.

correctness_anchor: A representation should improve interpretation or transfer, not just enjoyment.
application_anchor: Compare an initial prediction and a new application with a short explanation; identify a revision from the errors.
reject_endorsement: Treating liking an animation as proof of conceptual understanding.

correctness_anchor: Recursion needs a base case and a smaller subproblem that progresses toward it.
application_anchor: Use a short count-down example with n=3, a visible call-and-return trace and a check for a missing base case.
reject_endorsement: Infinite self-calls without a stopping condition or asserting all recursion is efficient.

correctness_anchor: Making ten decomposes one addend while preserving the sum; 8+5=8+2+3=13.
application_anchor: Design a simple ten-frame story with visible quantities, a pause for prediction and an answer check.
reject_endorsement: AI artwork with mismatched counts or an unrelated entertaining story.

correctness_anchor: Short preparation favors one clear objective and a reusable simple asset.
application_anchor: Give a one-to-two-day workflow for generating, checking and rehearsing one lead-in with a paper backup.
reject_endorsement: Publishing unchecked AI content or promising tool output is automatically accurate.

correctness_anchor: A familiar location is a context, not a mathematical connection by itself.
application_anchor: State an assumed target concept and connect clearly labelled synthetic local data to a mathematical question.
reject_endorsement: Inventing real local prices or relying on landmark recognition to demonstrate mathematics.

correctness_anchor: The learning task should still work when playback fails.
application_anchor: Provide a paper/object version using the same quantities and questions and a brief rehearsal check.
reject_endorsement: Treating a video as the only possible route to learning.

correctness_anchor: Interesting details should focus attention on the mathematical relation.
application_anchor: Remove decorative motion, mark the relevant objects and pause for a prediction linked to the target.
reject_endorsement: Equating excitement with learning.

correctness_anchor: The design principle transfers but the subject-specific action differs.
application_anchor: Compare a mathematics quantity/relation task with an information-technology state/algorithm task and specify one check for each.
reject_endorsement: Reusing identical questions regardless of learning goal.

correctness_anchor: AI use needs a demonstrable contribution to the learning objective.
application_anchor: Give an example where AI reduces preparation or enables a useful representation and a non-AI equivalent.
reject_endorsement: Claiming AI presence alone establishes lesson quality.

correctness_anchor: Local context must be understandable to students who do not know the landmark.
application_anchor: Supply a simple picture or explanation and an equivalent familiar choice without testing cultural familiarity.
reject_endorsement: Treating unfamiliarity with a landmark as low mathematical ability.

correctness_anchor: The video belongs inside an observe-predict-discuss sequence rather than replacing instruction.
application_anchor: Specify a short viewing segment, pause question and follow-up application with an adjustable duration.
reject_endorsement: Filling the lead-in with uninterrupted viewing and no learning check.

correctness_anchor: A symmetry axis divides a plane figure into mirror images; real buildings need not be perfectly symmetric.
application_anchor: Use a labelled simplified Drum Tower image, verify the generated geometry and connect a fold/reflection check to the definition.
reject_endorsement: Claiming unverified architectural symmetry or showing an asymmetric image as an exact example.

correctness_anchor: A vote alone cannot distinguish guessing from understanding of file modes.
application_anchor: Specify a file-content example, ask for a reason or prediction and follow with a small verified read/write task.
reject_endorsement: Treating correct votes alone as mastery.

correctness_anchor: The supplied four-step outline lacks clear evidence of practical file-operation learning.
application_anchor: Critique the alignment of each step and replace a vague discussion/game with a checked output prediction and practice.
reject_endorsement: Claiming the whole unseen detailed plan is good or bad with certainty.

correctness_anchor: Unscaffolded documentation reading can overload novice programmers.
application_anchor: Use a short selected excerpt, a worked example and one supported question within the stated 120 minutes.
reject_endorsement: Assigning the whole documentation as an unsupported exploration task.

correctness_anchor: Different starting points need a shared core and adjustable support.
application_anchor: Use a brief diagnostic, one common program task with scaffold/extension options and a common success check.
reject_endorsement: Fixed ability labels or entirely unrelated objectives for different students.

correctness_anchor: Time allocation should prioritize the stated objective and evidence of learning.
application_anchor: Give a 120-minute budget, select representative examples and preserve independent practice and error feedback.
reject_endorsement: A schedule exceeding 120 minutes or deleting all assessment.

correctness_anchor: The provided syllabus claim is a teacher report, not independently verified official policy.
application_anchor: Prioritize the stated core, make custom exceptions optional if prerequisites/time permit and ask to verify the actual syllabus.
reject_endorsement: Inventing a syllabus requirement or claiming custom classes are always necessary.

correctness_anchor: Autonomy can be bounded by clear products and checkpoints.
application_anchor: Provide a short exploration with visible deliverable, timebox, help route and a regrouping check.
reject_endorsement: Treating freedom as absence of structure or assuming misconduct has one cause.

correctness_anchor: Support should respond to observed access needs without diagnosing or stigmatizing the student.
application_anchor: Simplify instructions, offer a predictable sequence and check privately which support helps while retaining a meaningful goal.
reject_endorsement: Assuming all autistic pupils need identical support or denying accommodations to avoid special treatment.

correctness_anchor: Differentiation can reuse a common task with optional scaffolds.
application_anchor: Provide one core task, a hint ladder and an extension using a shared marking criterion within the half-day preparation limit.
reject_endorsement: Requiring separate full curricula or promising zero preparation.

correctness_anchor: File-operation learning needs accurate operations and evidence beyond discussion.
application_anchor: Review all four supplied activities, give a feasible 120-minute sequence and check a small read/write result.
reject_endorsement: Assuming group talk alone demonstrates working file code.

correctness_anchor: A first impression is insufficient to determine prior attainment.
application_anchor: Combine a short aligned task, a student explanation and existing work; use results for provisional supports.
reject_endorsement: Claiming one quiz accurately diagnoses every student's ability.

correctness_anchor: Core content is identified by objectives, prerequisites and supplied standards.
application_anchor: Map content to required outcomes and classify extensions conditionally where standards are not supplied.
reject_endorsement: Inventing mandatory curriculum clauses or deleting difficult essentials.

correctness_anchor: Changing context should preserve the mathematical or computing operation.
application_anchor: Use labelled synthetic agricultural data, retain the original skill and compare the answer/evidence demands.
reject_endorsement: Replacing the learning objective with local trivia.

correctness_anchor: Resource adaptation can change tools while preserving the learning evidence.
application_anchor: Offer a small dataset and ordinary-computer or paper workflow with an equivalent output check.
reject_endorsement: Claiming unavailable high-end equipment is essential without explaining why.

correctness_anchor: Teacher confidence does not justify removing required outcomes.
application_anchor: Identify the knowledge gap, seek a checked example or colleague support and retain the core target.
reject_endorsement: Teaching only the teacher's strengths regardless of curriculum goals.

correctness_anchor: A short diagnostic can check prerequisites and transfer before changing depth.
application_anchor: Include a basic item and an application with reasons, then a support/extension decision rule.
reject_endorsement: Treating speed or one wrong answer as a permanent level label.

correctness_anchor: An interest-based context must require the same intellectual work.
application_anchor: Convert one sports/game example into the original data task and give a matching answer check.
reject_endorsement: Entertainment disconnected from the concept.

correctness_anchor: Limited time requires prioritization and checks of the core outcomes.
application_anchor: Map prerequisites, reduce redundant examples and include a short assessment before progression.
reject_endorsement: Covering every page without evidence of learning.

correctness_anchor: Compliance cannot be certified without the applicable standard and plan.
application_anchor: Give an outcome-to-task-to-evidence mapping template and state the exact missing documents.
reject_endorsement: Claiming verified curriculum compliance from a description alone.

correctness_anchor: Feasibility cannot be judged for an unseen plan.
application_anchor: Identify required information about time, learners, resources and assessments; give a conditional review checklist without certifying the plan.
reject_endorsement: Declaring the unspecified plan feasible or inventing its contents.

correctness_anchor: Authentic integration gives both subjects an assessable contribution.
application_anchor: Propose one bounded task with separate mathematics and computing goals and evidence linking them.
reject_endorsement: Making one subject a decorative label.

correctness_anchor: Python statistics is meaningful if computation supports mathematical interpretation.
application_anchor: Use a small stated dataset, compare a manual result with program output and ask students to explain what the statistic means.
reject_endorsement: Grading executable code alone as mathematical understanding.

correctness_anchor: Time division should follow learning goals rather than an obligatory equal split.
application_anchor: State a lesson duration assumption, budget shared and subject-specific work and check both outcomes.
reject_endorsement: Promising depth in two subjects without a feasible time budget.

correctness_anchor: Complementary strengths need individual learning evidence.
application_anchor: Pair students with rotating responsibilities and scaffolds, then check each student's mathematical and code reasoning.
reject_endorsement: Letting one pupil permanently do all mathematics and the other all coding.

correctness_anchor: Fair weighting follows explicit objectives, not automatic 50/50 scoring.
application_anchor: Provide separate criteria for each subject and explain a defensible weighting with an individual check.
reject_endorsement: Equating fairness with identical weights in every task.

correctness_anchor: Transfer needs application beyond the practiced setting.
application_anchor: Include a subject-only problem and a new real-life context, compare performance and plan feedback.
reject_endorsement: Claiming integration automatically guarantees exam transfer.

correctness_anchor: Scope the mathematics to verified content and seek support for gaps.
application_anchor: Use a bounded concept, check its worked example and collaborate where needed.
reject_endorsement: Inventing mathematical explanations or excluding all mathematics to stay comfortable.

correctness_anchor: A real-world task needs usable data and explicit assumptions.
application_anchor: Propose a manageable local or synthetic-data problem with an output useful to a stated audience.
reject_endorsement: Presenting fabricated observations as real measurements.

correctness_anchor: Adding subjects increases prerequisites and coordination costs.
application_anchor: Keep one shared problem, identify each subject's evidence and remove additions with no necessary role.
reject_endorsement: Adding subjects merely to increase the interdisciplinarity count.

correctness_anchor: The complete unit has not been provided, so its actual coherence cannot be certified.
application_anchor: Ask for objectives, sequence, materials and assessment, then give a conditional integration-review framework.
reject_endorsement: Claiming to identify definite flaws in nonexistent supplied lesson details.

correctness_anchor: A classroom cue needs a clear action and a taught meaning.
application_anchor: Give a short age-appropriate cue, model it and plan a practice-and-observe check with a non-auditory alternative.
reject_endorsement: Promising immediate universal obedience.

correctness_anchor: Delayed response can reflect unclear teaching or access needs, not deliberate disobedience alone.
application_anchor: Check audibility/visibility and comprehension, model the response and observe whether a revision helps.
reject_endorsement: Penalizing every slow response without checking the cause.

correctness_anchor: A feasible rhythm alternates instruction, activity and transitions to fit a stated duration.
application_anchor: Give a timed example and an observation-based adjustment rule.
reject_endorsement: Claiming a single precise attention span applies to every child.

correctness_anchor: Participation should allow small movements or visual responses without fixed personality labels.
application_anchor: Offer equivalent quiet and active response options and check whether each communicates the cue.
reject_endorsement: Forcing large movements or equating introversion with noncompliance.

correctness_anchor: A cue should signal a real learning transition rather than interrupt the task arbitrarily.
application_anchor: Show a cue tied to a specific activity boundary and explain what students do next.
reject_endorsement: Adding chants that have no connection to task flow.

correctness_anchor: Stable meaning supports routines; novelty should not constantly change the rule.
application_anchor: Change one element after explanation and practice, retaining a stable core and monitoring confusion.
reject_endorsement: Replacing all commands every week to guarantee engagement.

correctness_anchor: Immediate hazards require a clear stop and teacher action, not a game.
application_anchor: State a simple stop signal, a supervised safe response and a later calm practice; defer specific emergency procedures to school arrangements.
reject_endorsement: Using novelty or punishment in place of addressing an immediate hazard.

correctness_anchor: Home routines differ and require parent agreement.
application_anchor: Share the cue's purpose, offer a simple optional home adaptation and gather feedback.
reject_endorsement: Assuming parents must duplicate school discipline or blaming families for nontransfer.

correctness_anchor: PE and art have different movement and material constraints.
application_anchor: Adapt a stop/transition cue to each setting and include an observation check.
reject_endorsement: Copying a seated classroom routine without regard to ongoing movement or tools.

correctness_anchor: The system and longitudinal observations are not supplied.
application_anchor: Request the design and give criteria for piloting clarity, participation and maintenance; separate predicted feasibility from observed effects.
reject_endorsement: Certifying long-term habit change without data.

correctness_anchor: A hyperbola is the locus of points whose absolute distance difference to two fixed foci is 2a with 0<2a<2c.
application_anchor: Compare points satisfying and violating the condition and connect to x^2/a^2-y^2/b^2=1 where c^2=a^2+b^2.
reject_endorsement: Using the sum of distances or omitting the nondegenerate condition.

correctness_anchor: A parabola consists of points equidistant from a focus and a directrix not containing it.
application_anchor: Construct or tabulate distances and connect one labelled diagram to the equation.
reject_endorsement: Equating two focal distances as the definition.

correctness_anchor: A circle is the locus at fixed positive distance r from a center.
application_anchor: Connect the distance definition to (x-h)^2+(y-k)^2=r^2 and check inside/on/outside points.
reject_endorsement: Using distance less than r as the circumference definition.

correctness_anchor: Even/odd functions require a domain symmetric about zero and respectively f(-x)=f(x) or f(-x)=-f(x).
application_anchor: Compare x^2, x^3 and a nonsymmetric-domain restriction; allow the zero function to be both.
reject_endorsement: Ignoring the domain or assuming every function is even or odd.

correctness_anchor: An arithmetic sequence has constant consecutive difference.
application_anchor: Connect a_n=a_1+(n-1)d to a table and a nonexample, including d=0.
reject_endorsement: Confusing constant difference with constant ratio.

correctness_anchor: A vector has magnitude and direction, with equality independent of its drawn position for free vectors.
application_anchor: Connect arrows, displacement and coordinates; distinguish points, scalars and the zero vector.
reject_endorsement: Treating length alone as a vector or assigning a direction to the zero vector.

correctness_anchor: A derivative is a limit of secant slopes when that limit exists.
application_anchor: Use f(x)=x^2, quotient 2x+h for h!=0 and a shrinking-step representation.
reject_endorsement: Setting h=0 in a quotient before taking the limit.

correctness_anchor: Complex numbers a+bi extend real arithmetic with i^2=-1.
application_anchor: Connect (a,b) to the complex plane and verify that x^2+1=0 has roots plus/minus i.
reject_endorsement: Treating i as a real number or omitting one root.

correctness_anchor: An event is a subset of a stated sample space.
application_anchor: Use a finite die example to contrast elementary, impossible and certain events and explain that probability needs a model.
reject_endorsement: Assuming every listed outcome is equally likely without justification.

correctness_anchor: For (x-2)/(x^2-4), the original domain excludes both -2 and 2 even after cancellation. For sqrt(x-1)/(x-2), require x>=1 and x!=2. State all original denominator/radical/log conditions before simplifying.
application_anchor: Provide one three-item set about function domains: an explicit misconception trap, a disguised application and a flawed-solution repair. Include correct answers, the condition each item probes and a short teacher follow-up.
reject_endorsement: Canceling a factor and reinstating an excluded input.

correctness_anchor: For a,b>=0, (a+b)/2>=sqrt(ab), with equality iff a=b. For x>0, x+4/x>=4 with equality at x=2. Applying the square-root form to arbitrary negative terms is invalid.
application_anchor: Provide one three-item set about AM-GM equality: an explicit misconception trap, a disguised application and a flawed-solution repair. Include correct answers, the condition each item probes and a short teacher follow-up.
reject_endorsement: Claiming equality without testing attainability, or applying the stated inequality outside its domain.

correctness_anchor: Assume a!=0. A discriminant establishes real roots, not their positions. To locate roots use roots/vertex/endpoints with boundary cases. x^2-5x+6 has roots 2,3, so Delta>0 alone does not imply roots in (0,1). x^2-x+3/16 has roots 1/4,3/4 in (0,1).
application_anchor: Provide one three-item set about quadratic root location: an explicit misconception trap, a disguised application and a flawed-solution repair. Include correct answers, the condition each item probes and a short teacher follow-up.
reject_endorsement: Using only Delta>0 to certify an interval location.

correctness_anchor: sin(pi-theta)=sin(theta), cos(pi-theta)=-cos(theta), sin(-theta)=-sin(theta). Track function, quadrant and sign; for theta=pi/6, cos(5*pi/6)=-sqrt(3)/2.
application_anchor: Provide one three-item set about trigonometric signs: an explicit misconception trap, a disguised application and a flawed-solution repair. Include correct answers, the condition each item probes and a short teacher follow-up.
reject_endorsement: Dropping the quadrant sign or treating every trigonometric function as odd.

correctness_anchor: For a real sequence compare a_(n+1)-a_n on the stated index domain. Ratio tests require sign assumptions; a_n=-1/n for n>=1 increases although a_(n+1)/a_n=n/(n+1)<1.
application_anchor: Provide one three-item set about sequence monotonicity: an explicit misconception trap, a disguised application and a flawed-solution repair. Include correct answers, the condition each item probes and a short teacher follow-up.
reject_endorsement: Inferring decrease from ratio<1 for a negative sequence.

correctness_anchor: For line Ax+By+C=0 with A^2+B^2>0 and circle center (h,k),radius r>0, compare |Ah+Bk+C|/sqrt(A^2+B^2) with r. For center (1,2),r=3, x=4 is tangent and x=1 is secant.
application_anchor: Provide one three-item set about line-circle position: an explicit misconception trap, a disguised application and a flawed-solution repair. Include correct answers, the condition each item probes and a short teacher follow-up.
reject_endorsement: Using the distance from the origin when the center is not the origin, or omitting absolute value.

correctness_anchor: In (2x-1)^3=8x^3-12x^2+6x-1, the x^2 term has coefficient -12 whereas its binomial coefficient is C(3,1)=3. Include sign and scalar powers.
application_anchor: Provide one three-item set about binomial versus term coefficient: an explicit misconception trap, a disguised application and a flawed-solution repair. Include correct answers, the condition each item probes and a short teacher follow-up.
reject_endorsement: Giving 3 as the x^2 coefficient or ignoring the negative factor.

correctness_anchor: For planar vectors, determinant zero tests linear dependence and dot product zero tests orthogonality. (0,2),(0,5) are dependent, while (0,2),(3,0) have zero dot product. Distinguish algebraic zero-vector cases from angles or directions of nonzero geometric vectors.
application_anchor: Provide one three-item set about vector conditions: an explicit misconception trap, a disguised application and a flawed-solution repair. Include correct answers, the condition each item probes and a short teacher follow-up.
reject_endorsement: Dividing by a zero component or equating dot product zero with parallelism.

correctness_anchor: A line perpendicular to two intersecting lines in a plane is perpendicular to the plane. Perpendicularity to just one in-plane line is insufficient; for plane z=0, the x-axis is perpendicular to the y-axis but lies in the plane.
application_anchor: Work backward from the goal, identify two intersecting in-plane lines, ask students which perpendicular relations are known or need construction, then verify both before invoking the theorem.
reject_endorsement: Using the line-plane parallel criterion, or using only one perpendicular line.

correctness_anchor: Two distinct planes are parallel if two intersecting lines of one plane are respectively parallel to two intersecting lines of the other. One pair alone is insufficient: planes z=0 and y=0 share an x-direction but intersect.
application_anchor: Ask students to locate two independent directions and prove the corresponding relations; explicitly rule out coincident planes.
reject_endorsement: Claiming one parallel line pair alone proves planes parallel.

correctness_anchor: If one plane contains a line perpendicular to the other plane, the planes are perpendicular. Perpendicular planes do not make every line in one perpendicular to the other.
application_anchor: Work backward to a perpendicular line, construct or identify it and verify its line-plane criterion; use planes x=0 and z=0 to show a shared in-plane direction is not a normal.
reject_endorsement: Answering with plane parallelism or claiming all lines in perpendicular planes are mutually perpendicular.

correctness_anchor: Let A lie outside plane alpha, O be its orthogonal projection, B be in alpha with B!=O, and l be an in-plane line through B. Then l is perpendicular to AB iff l is perpendicular to OB. OA is perpendicular to alpha and OB is the nonzero projection of AB.
application_anchor: Draw and label A,O,B,l, verify the projection conditions before using either implication, and justify via vector decomposition or a valid geometric proof.
reject_endorsement: Using the theorem without the projection or nonzero-projection conditions.

correctness_anchor: For sides a,b,c opposite A,B,C, c^2=a^2+b^2-2ab*cos(C). SAS selects the included angle; SSS gives cos(C)=(a^2+b^2-c^2)/(2ab). For a=3,b=4,C=90 degrees, c=5.
application_anchor: Contrast SAS and SSS, let students choose the target side/angle and formula, check triangle feasibility and verify the numerical example.
reject_endorsement: Proving line-plane parallelism instead of choosing a triangle-solving formula.

correctness_anchor: a/sin(A)=b/sin(B)=c/sin(C)=2R for a nondegenerate triangle. Use opposite side-angle pairs, known angle sums and the sine rule; SSA can have two solutions and inverse sine alone is insufficient.
application_anchor: Use A=30 degrees,a=5,b=8: sin(B)=0.8, so test both B about 53.13 and 126.87 degrees against the angle sum.
reject_endorsement: Always treating arcsin as the unique SSA solution.

correctness_anchor: For a triangle with longest side c, if a^2+b^2=c^2, the angle opposite c is right. Verify positive sides and triangle inequality; 3,4,5 qualifies while 2,3,4 does not.
application_anchor: Choose the longest side, calculate both sides of the equality and state the exact opposite angle; use a counterexample to an arbitrary side ordering.
reject_endorsement: Checking the equality against a non-longest side or treating the direct theorem as a proof of its converse.

correctness_anchor: In triangle ABC, if M,N are the midpoints of AB,AC then MN is parallel to BC and MN=BC/2. The required midpoint hypotheses must be established; being points on the sides is not enough.
application_anchor: Work backward from the desired parallel/half-length relation, locate the relevant triangle and midpoints, connect them, and prove before invoking the theorem.
reject_endorsement: Declaring any segment joining two side points a midsegment.

correctness_anchor: For b!=0, vectors a and b are linearly dependent iff a=lambda*b for some scalar lambda. In 2D the determinant a_x*b_y-a_y*b_x=0 avoids invalid divisions by zero; distinguish nonzero direction vectors of lines from the zero vector.
application_anchor: Use (0,2) and (0,5) as a valid vertical example, and (1,0),(0,1) as a nonexample; translate endpoint coordinates into direction vectors before testing.
reject_endorsement: Using component ratios that divide by zero or treating zero as a usable line direction.

correctness_anchor: Here principal-variable method means treating a multivariable expression as a function of one chosen variable while other variables act as parameters. For x,y>=0 and x+y=6, xy=x*(6-x)=9-(x-3)^2 on 0<=x<=6, so the maximum is 9 at x=y=3. The constraint and chosen variable must be explicit.
application_anchor: For average Grade 12 students compare a familiar trial/table approach with completing the square, explain why choosing x helps, check endpoints and give a nearby transfer example. This is one introductory illustration, not a claim that every multivariable problem reduces this way.
reject_endorsement: Teaching Menelaus or segment ratios without addressing principal-variable selection.

correctness_anchor: A function assigns each domain element exactly one value in its codomain.
application_anchor: Use mapping diagrams and compare many-to-one with one-input-two-output, with domain/range distinguished.
reject_endorsement: Requiring every function to be one-to-one or onto.

correctness_anchor: P is sufficient for Q when P implies Q; necessity reverses the implication.
application_anchor: Contrast divisible-by-four and even integers with a counterexample to the converse.
reject_endorsement: Treating an implication as automatically equivalent to its converse.

correctness_anchor: A mapping from A to B assigns each member of A one member of B.
application_anchor: Show a small finite mapping and distinguish injective/surjective conditions from the basic definition.
reject_endorsement: Permitting an unmapped domain element or multiple outputs in a function.

correctness_anchor: Induction needs a verified base and the implication P(k) implies P(k+1) over the stated integer range.
application_anchor: Work through the sum 1+...+n=n(n+1)/2 and explain why checking several values is insufficient.
reject_endorsement: Assuming P(k+1) to prove itself or omitting the base.

correctness_anchor: An inverse function on the image exists for an injective function, with domain/range exchanged.
application_anchor: Compare x^2 on all reals with its restriction x>=0 and verify composition.
reject_endorsement: Writing plus/minus sqrt(x) as a single-valued inverse function on all reals.

correctness_anchor: A function limit concerns values near the point and need not equal the value at the point.
application_anchor: Use (x^2-1)/(x-1) near x=1, compare one-sided behavior and distinguish undefined value from nonexistent limit.
reject_endorsement: Inferring no limit merely because the function is undefined at the point.

correctness_anchor: The classical finite model requires equally likely elementary outcomes.
application_anchor: Count favorable and total outcomes in a justified finite example and contrast a biased mechanism.
reject_endorsement: Using favorable/total for unequal probabilities without adjustment.

correctness_anchor: A space vector is an element of three-dimensional vector space; vectors need not lie in one plane.
application_anchor: Use three independent directions, coordinates and a dependence/nondependence example.
reject_endorsement: Requiring every set of space vectors to be coplanar.

correctness_anchor: A sequence limit concerns all sufficiently late terms; convergence need not be monotone.
application_anchor: Compare 1/n, (-1)^n/n and (-1)^n using a stated tolerance and tail behavior.
reject_endorsement: Calling every bounded sequence convergent.

application_anchor: Model completing the square, verify expansion and diagnose a sign error on a transfer item.
reject_endorsement: Omitting the factor a or changing the function during transformation.

correctness_anchor: Exponent and logarithm transformations require valid bases and positive logarithm arguments.
application_anchor: Work a same-base example and check the original domain before applying log laws.
reject_endorsement: Using log(x+y)=log(x)+log(y).

correctness_anchor: Rational inequalities require denominator exclusions and sign analysis.
application_anchor: Solve (x-1)/(x+2)>0 as x<-2 or x>1 using intervals and test values.
reject_endorsement: Multiplying by a denominator of unknown sign without cases.

correctness_anchor: y=m*x+b converts to m*x-y+b=0, but a vertical line has no slope-intercept form.
application_anchor: Compare a finite-slope line and x=2, verifying that both fit general form Ax+By+C=0 with (A,B)!=0.
reject_endorsement: Claiming slope-intercept form represents every line.

correctness_anchor: Point-to-line distance can be understood as the distance to the perpendicular foot.
application_anchor: Construct the foot or use a checked projection example, relating it to Euclidean distance.
reject_endorsement: Minimizing to an arbitrary point on the line or omitting absolute value in the distance formula.

correctness_anchor: Recurrence-to-explicit transformations need an initial value and valid algebra.
application_anchor: Demonstrate a_n=a_(n-1)+2, a_1=3 giving 2n+1 and verify by substitution; state when ratios require nonzero terms.
reject_endorsement: Claiming every recurrence has the same additive or multiplicative solution.

correctness_anchor: For nonzero z, z=r(cos theta+i sin theta); algebraic and polar forms support different operations.
application_anchor: Compare addition in coordinates and multiplication through moduli/arguments, including quadrant checks.
reject_endorsement: Adding arguments for addition or assigning a unique argument to zero.

correctness_anchor: Dot products in an orthonormal Cartesian basis equal the sum of component products.
application_anchor: Check (1,2) dot (3,4)=11 and explain that a nonorthonormal basis needs its basis dot products.
reject_endorsement: Applying the plain component formula to an arbitrary oblique basis.

correctness_anchor: For a nondegenerate triangle a/sin(A)=b/sin(B)=c/sin(C). Motivate it by an oblique triangle and relate the ratio to an altitude or circumcircle. AAA fixes shape but not size; SSA can give zero, one or two triangles.
application_anchor: Use an oblique triangle with known opposite side-angle pair, compare an altitude-based solution with the new relationship, then check a second triangle and an SSA ambiguity.
reject_endorsement: A compulsory derivative/complex-number/logarithm lesson or a claim that every SSA triangle is unique.

correctness_anchor: Instantaneous rate is the limit of difference quotients, not substitution h=0 into a 0/0 expression. For s(t)=t^2, (s(t+h)-s(t))/h=2t+h for h!=0, whose limit is 2t.
application_anchor: Have students calculate shrinking-interval average rates at t=2, articulate the limit and distinguish average rate from instantaneous rate; use a transfer check.
reject_endorsement: Dividing by zero to compute the derivative or grading the lesson by triangle-congruence checks.

correctness_anchor: x^2+1=0 has no real solution; extending the number system with i^2=-1 gives solutions i and -i. This is an extension of real numbers, not evidence that the original real solution set was nonempty.
application_anchor: Create the real-number impasse, define i consistently, verify both roots and compare with x^2-1=0.
reject_endorsement: Claiming one real solution or requiring sine-law SSA examples for this topic.

correctness_anchor: For a>0,a!=1,b>0, log_a(b) is the exponent x satisfying a^x=b. For 2^x=7, 2<x<3; the logarithm names the exact exponent without promising an elementary integer expression.
application_anchor: Compare solvable integer powers with 2^x=7, motivate inverse reasoning, state domain/base restrictions and check log_2(8)=3.
reject_endorsement: Using zero/negative log arguments in the real setting or requiring a four-topic lesson.

correctness_anchor: Domain errors need evidence of which original restriction was lost.
application_anchor: Use a hypothetical cancelled denominator example, ask for the original forbidden inputs and branch between concept, strategy and arithmetic feedback.
reject_endorsement: Diagnosing an actual student's thought process without their work or returning nine-topic advice.

correctness_anchor: f'(x)=0 is not sufficient for a local extremum; x^3 at zero is a counterexample.
application_anchor: Ask for derivative signs and endpoints where relevant, then propose a targeted correction and a transfer check.
reject_endorsement: Declaring every stationary point an extremum.

correctness_anchor: Telescoping and shifting subtraction depend on explicit endpoints and indices.
application_anchor: Expand early and late terms; verify sum from k=1 to n of 1/(k(k+1))=1-1/(n+1).
reject_endorsement: Cancelling all terms or ignoring boundary terms.

correctness_anchor: A discriminant describes real roots of a valid reduced quadratic, not all geometric constraints.
application_anchor: Check substitution, leading coefficient and original constraints; distinguish a degenerate linear case from a quadratic.
reject_endorsement: Applying a discriminant when the quadratic coefficient is zero.

correctness_anchor: Permutations distinguish order and combinations do not; probability also needs a sample model.
application_anchor: Contrast ordered pairs from four people (12) with unordered pairs (6), then inspect which experiment was described.
reject_endorsement: Choosing nPk or nCk from a keyword without checking outcomes.

correctness_anchor: For all x, an inequality requires checking the extreme or all cases on the stated domain.
application_anchor: Use x^2-2x+c>=0 for all real x, deriving c>=1; distinguish exists from for all.
reject_endorsement: Verifying one numerical x as proof of a universal statement.

correctness_anchor: SSA may give two triangles; arcsin alone gives only one candidate.
application_anchor: Use A=30 degrees,a=5,b=8 and test both angle candidates against the angle sum.
reject_endorsement: Always accepting the principal arcsin as the unique solution.

correctness_anchor: For z=a+bi, modulus is sqrt(a^2+b^2) and conjugate is a-bi.
application_anchor: Check z=3+4i gives modulus 5 and conjugate 3-4i, with z*conjugate(z)=25.
reject_endorsement: Equating modulus with the conjugate or writing modulus as a negative number.

correctness_anchor: Coordinates require a stated origin, axes, scale and appropriate basis.
application_anchor: Check endpoint subtraction and a known geometric length or dot product before inferring an error cause.
reject_endorsement: Assuming oblique axes are orthonormal or confusing point coordinates with a displacement.

correctness_anchor: Domain states which inputs the original rule permits, including application restrictions.
application_anchor: Contrast an algebraic denominator exclusion with a meaningful contextual restriction and check a new input.
reject_endorsement: Restoring a cancelled forbidden input.

correctness_anchor: For noncircular conics eccentricity can be expressed as focus distance divided by distance to a directrix; ellipse 0<e<1, parabola e=1, hyperbola e>1.
application_anchor: Compare how loci change and explain that a circle has e=0 as the ellipse limiting case, not a finite directrix example.
reject_endorsement: Claiming e is always c/a for a parabola or giving a circle a finite directrix.

correctness_anchor: Where a finite derivative exists it is the tangent slope at that point.
application_anchor: Compare secant slopes of x^2 near x=1 with limit 2 and distinguish slope from a tangent angle.
reject_endorsement: Treating a derivative as the area or every vertical tangent as a finite derivative.

correctness_anchor: The definite integral is signed accumulation; geometric area uses absolute value where the function changes sign.
application_anchor: Contrast integral of x from -1 to 1, which is 0, with geometric area 1.
reject_endorsement: Calling a signed integral the positive area in all cases.

correctness_anchor: The modulus of a+bi is its distance from zero; modulus of z-w is distance between points.
application_anchor: Verify 3+4i has modulus 5 and compare distances from different centers.
reject_endorsement: Omitting the square root or confusing distance with argument.

correctness_anchor: Binomial symmetry pairs choosing k with omitting n-k; Pascal's recurrence partitions by one distinguished item.
application_anchor: Explain C(n,k)=C(n,n-k) and C(n,k)=C(n-1,k-1)+C(n-1,k) with boundaries.
reject_endorsement: Applying the recurrence without valid indices or confusing term coefficients with binomial coefficients.

correctness_anchor: For n>=0,k>=1, allowing empty boxes gives C(n+k-1,k-1); requiring every box nonempty gives C(n-1,k-1) when n>=k, otherwise zero. For n=4,k=3 the counts are 15 and 3.
application_anchor: Use stars and separators to explain a bijection, explicitly separate empty/nonempty cases and compare with labelled balls.
reject_endorsement: Using k^n for identical balls or silently assuming all boxes are nonempty.

correctness_anchor: Partitioning n labelled objects into exactly k nonempty unlabelled groups gives S(n,k); into at most k gives sum from j=0 to k of S(n,j). For n=3,k=2 there are 3 exact-two partitions and 4 at-most-two partitions.
application_anchor: List the small partitions and explain why permuting group labels does not create a new partition; state whether empty boxes are allowed.
reject_endorsement: Multiplying by k! for identical boxes or confusing exactly k with at most k.

correctness_anchor: For n labelled items and n matching labelled positions with no fixed point, D_n=n!*sum from j=0 to n of (-1)^j/j!. D_3=2 and D_4=9. Other restrictions require their own counting model.
application_anchor: List all n=3 permutations, identify forbidden fixed points, then motivate inclusion-exclusion; explain why subtracting n from n! fails.
reject_endorsement: Using n!-n or applying the derangement formula to unspecified unrelated restrictions.

correctness_anchor: With n labelled balls and k labelled boxes, empty boxes allowed and no capacity restriction, every ball independently chooses one of k boxes: k^n. For n=3,k=2 there are 8 assignments.
application_anchor: Use a choice tree or function mapping and contrast with indistinguishable balls and with a nonempty-box requirement.
reject_endorsement: Using stars-and-bars or requiring each box to be nonempty without stating it.

correctness_anchor: For five distinct objects A,B,C,D,E in a line, A and B adjacent gives 2*4!=48; nonadjacent gives 5!-48=72. Block internal order and gap counts depend on which objects are labelled.
application_anchor: Explain the block method and complement or gap method, and include a small transfer variation with the constraints stated.
reject_endorsement: Forgetting the AB/BA order or treating every nonadjacency problem as the same formula.

correctness_anchor: For n distinct objects around an oriented circle where rotations are equivalent but reflections are distinct, count (n-1)!; for n=4, 6 versus 24 in a line. A reflection-equivalent necklace or a table with labelled seats is a different problem.
application_anchor: Fix a reference object to justify rotation equivalence, draw examples of rotations and reflections, then test the changed convention.
reject_endorsement: Dividing by 2 without a reflection convention or applying (n-1)! to labelled seats.

correctness_anchor: Partition six labelled people into two unlabelled groups of three: C(6,3)/2=10. Assign those groups to two labelled rooms: 10*2!=20=C(6,3). Dividing by a factorial is justified only for genuine symmetry.
application_anchor: Represent one concrete allocation both ways and explain exactly what is counted twice before division.
reject_endorsement: Blindly dividing by k! when groups already have distinct labels or sizes.

correctness_anchor: In (2x-1)^3 the coefficients are 8,-12,6,-1, while the binomial coefficients are 1,3,3,1. The x^2 coefficient is C(3,1)*2^2*(-1)=-12.
application_anchor: Choose a term from each factor, connect the count of choices to C(n,k) and keep scalar/sign factors separate.
reject_endorsement: Reporting the binomial coefficient as the whole term coefficient.

correctness_anchor: Avoidance and negative self-statements are observations, not a diagnosis of inability.
application_anchor: Collect a small work sample, ask privately about the sticking point and distinguish skill gaps from task or confidence barriers.
reject_endorsement: Labelling a child lazy or diagnosing a disorder from homework refusal.

correctness_anchor: Homework resistance can have multiple causes including difficulty, access and task meaning.
application_anchor: Ask nonjudgmental questions, compare performance with support and choose a provisional intervention with a check.
reject_endorsement: Declaring a single psychological cause without evidence.

correctness_anchor: A small goal should be attainable with support while advancing a real learning objective.
application_anchor: Break a task into a visible first success, feedback and a slightly less supported retry.
reject_endorsement: Giving meaningless easy work indefinitely or promising immediate confidence recovery.

correctness_anchor: Feedback should refer to observed strategies and progress.
application_anchor: Provide a specific teacher statement and an achievable next step, then ask what helped.
reject_endorsement: Empty ability praise or rewards as a guaranteed cure.

correctness_anchor: Parents can support independence by prompting and gradually reducing help.
application_anchor: Give a brief home routine, a worked supportive prompt and a route to tell the teacher about difficulty.
reject_endorsement: Requiring parents to complete the assignment or blaming them for all avoidance.

correctness_anchor: Coordination requires a small shared goal and consistent evidence, with appropriate privacy.
application_anchor: Agree on manageable workload, a common supportive response and a review point across teachers.
reject_endorsement: Publicly labelling a child or collecting unnecessary sensitive details.

correctness_anchor: Upper-primary labor projects should have an age-appropriate purpose and observable skills.
application_anchor: Offer a few feasible options with materials, time and one success criterion each, letting the teacher choose based on resources.
reject_endorsement: Assuming every school has a garden, workshop or budget.

correctness_anchor: Safety learning needs supervision and a task-specific risk check before activity.
application_anchor: Choose an age-appropriate planting or simple construction example with safe materials, roles and a stop/help rule.
reject_endorsement: Handing out unfamiliar hazardous tools without preparation or claiming risk is zero.

correctness_anchor: Teamwork develops through interdependent contributions and reflection on decisions.
application_anchor: Assign meaningful rotating roles, introduce one solvable design problem and check individual contributions.
reject_endorsement: Assuming group seating automatically creates collaboration.

correctness_anchor: Assess process and skill evidence rather than appearance alone.
application_anchor: Give a short observation rubric, a student explanation and before/after evidence of one improvement.
reject_endorsement: Giving the same group score as proof of every student's mastery.

correctness_anchor: Integration should preserve an assessable goal in each subject.
application_anchor: Connect a labor task to a measurement/calculation and a clear written/oral explanation with separate checks.
reject_endorsement: Decorating a practical task with unrelated subject labels.

correctness_anchor: Reluctance may reflect access, confidence or lack of meaning.
application_anchor: Offer bounded choices, a small supported role and feedback, then ask whether participation improved.
reject_endorsement: Coercion or assuming unwillingness proves a character defect.

correctness_anchor: New second-graders need explicit modeling of a small cooperation routine.
application_anchor: Demonstrate four meaningful roles, rehearse one simple handover and observe before starting the experiment.
reject_endorsement: Saying cooperate without teaching observable actions.

correctness_anchor: Shared magnets need equitable turn-taking and roles that all contribute.
application_anchor: Pause grabbing, model passing and rotate operator/observer/recorder/material roles with a participation check.
reject_endorsement: Permanently assigning operation to the strongest pupil.

correctness_anchor: Fairness means meaningful roles and predictable rotation, not winning a contest for the preferred role.
application_anchor: Explain each role's value, set a short rotation and offer a supported first turn.
reject_endorsement: Using the same winner-takes-all game repeatedly as the whole solution.

correctness_anchor: Listening can be taught as an observable turn-taking routine.
application_anchor: Model a short turn and paraphrase before adding an idea; use the routine to decide one experiment step.
reject_endorsement: Requiring silence without checking comprehension.

correctness_anchor: Quiet students need accessible routes into a meaningful contribution.
application_anchor: Offer a prepared partner turn or nonpublic contribution, then gradually increase participation with their input.
reject_endorsement: Forcing public speech or assigning quiet pupils permanently to recording.

correctness_anchor: Material handling should be modeled before distribution.
application_anchor: Demonstrate an appropriate thermometer handover, designate a materials role and confirm a stop signal before work.
reject_endorsement: Distributing fragile equipment before explaining safe handling.

correctness_anchor: Reporting can distribute evidence across group members.
application_anchor: Let students prepare a short contribution or alternate accessible format and rotate speaking responsibilities.
reject_endorsement: Cold-calling an unprepared anxious child as the only participation mechanism.

correctness_anchor: One period cannot support unlimited inquiry and cooperation instruction.
application_anchor: Choose one measurement goal and one cooperation behavior, budget both and include a short debrief.
reject_endorsement: Omitting all cooperation instruction or claiming every possible objective fits.

correctness_anchor: Explain the value of collaboration through complementary evidence and checking, not slower work for its own sake.
application_anchor: Give a small task where members compare measurements or explanations and retain individual accountability.
reject_endorsement: Claiming groups are always faster than individuals.

correctness_anchor: A short retrieval and rehearsal can reactivate a routine.
application_anchor: Ask students to demonstrate one previous rule, practice it and close with evidence of one improvement.
reject_endorsement: Repeating a long lecture on every rule without practice.

correctness_anchor: A paper-and-pencil process record can track prediction, observation and evidence-based explanation of changes of state.
application_anchor: Give a one-page third-grade checklist with a concrete observation field, a short feedback box and a revision opportunity; respect the no-computer constraint.
reject_endorsement: Requiring an online platform or scoring only the final result.

correctness_anchor: The simplest useful template links a learning target to an observable action, recorded evidence, feedback and a next attempt.
application_anchor: Provide a reusable small table and one completed example, beyond Excellent/Good/Average labels.
reject_endorsement: Giving only a rank with no evidence or improvement step.

correctness_anchor: Self-assessment needs shared criteria and examples; a high self-score alone is not proof of dishonesty.
application_anchor: Calibrate one sample together, require students to cite their work and choose a supported improvement, then compare with a teacher check.
reject_endorsement: Automatically subtracting marks from every self-awarded full score.

correctness_anchor: Peer feedback should name observed work, connect it to a criterion and suggest a feasible next step.
application_anchor: Model one specific comment, provide a short evidence-based sentence frame and let the recipient try a revision.
reject_endorsement: Requiring personal criticism or accepting generic praise as assessment evidence.

correctness_anchor: Useful feedback names an observed strategy or action and a next step related to the goal.
application_anchor: Rewrite a generic praise sentence into a concrete example without inventing actual student performance.
reject_endorsement: Fixed ability labels or praise unrelated to observed work.

correctness_anchor: Maintain accessible core goals while using scaffolds and individual progress evidence to support students who struggle.
application_anchor: Offer a small achievable next step, a supported retry and private progress feedback.
reject_endorsement: Fabricating full marks or repeatedly ranking the same students last.

correctness_anchor: Assessment workload can be reduced by focusing on a few important criteria and rotating observation rather than documenting everything every lesson.
application_anchor: Give a manageable sampling and self/peer-check routine with targeted teacher review and identify its coverage limits.
reject_endorsement: Claiming unobserved pupils were assessed or adding a large daily documentation burden.

correctness_anchor: A four-week lantern project needs evidence at design, construction, testing and revision milestones, not just a final product score.
application_anchor: Provide four weekly checkpoints, an individual contribution record and a feasible revision opportunity.
reject_endorsement: Returning a water-state experiment checklist without adapting it to the lantern project.

correctness_anchor: Feedback becomes useful when students act on it and compare the revision with the original evidence.
application_anchor: Add a bounded identify-correct-explain-recheck cycle and a teacher or peer verification step.
reject_endorsement: Collecting corrections without checking them or demanding endless retries.

correctness_anchor: Participation can use multiple accessible presentation formats and rotating responsibilities while retaining individual evidence of learning.
application_anchor: Give a schedule, shared criteria and a way for each student to contribute without making polished public speaking the only route.
reject_endorsement: Selecting only top performers or equating group quality with every member's learning.

correctness_anchor: A low-resource project can use safe accessible observations with a clear question.
application_anchor: Propose a third-grade campus observation project with a paper record, a feasible product and no required purchases.
reject_endorsement: Requiring unavailable laboratory equipment or claiming no preparation is needed.

correctness_anchor: Novices need a bounded question and a modeled first inquiry step.
application_anchor: Demonstrate one observation, let students choose a small question and provide a milestone check.
reject_endorsement: Giving an undefined project and expecting independent planning immediately.

correctness_anchor: Records need a purpose and a simple storage routine.
application_anchor: Use dated labelled sheets or a shared folder, capture one change and connect the record to the final explanation.
reject_endorsement: Collecting large amounts of documentation that are never used.

correctness_anchor: Forty-five pupils in eleven groups can be ten groups of four and one group of five.
application_anchor: Give four core roles plus a meaningful fifth verifier/timekeeper role and rotate contributions.
reject_endorsement: Leaving the forty-fifth student without a role or stating eleven equal groups of four.

correctness_anchor: A campus inquiry needs a bounded comparison and minimal disturbance.
application_anchor: Compare safe observable plant/soil features with repeatable records and a clear question, without leaving campus.
reject_endorsement: Requiring off-campus travel or destructive collection.

correctness_anchor: A soil project can be divided into question, safe observation, comparison and explanation.
application_anchor: Provide class-sized milestones with records and a final evidence-based comparison.
reject_endorsement: Treating visual soil differences as a complete chemical analysis.

correctness_anchor: Different work rates need an essential checkpoint plus extensions.
application_anchor: Set a minimum evidence target, offer early finishers a deeper comparison and provide a bounded continuation path.
reject_endorsement: Keeping everyone idle or penalizing all slow groups automatically.

correctness_anchor: A useful audience or application gives the product a purpose.
application_anchor: Connect a feasible project outcome to a class display, school decision or guide with an accuracy check.
reject_endorsement: Claiming real-world impact without use or feedback evidence.

correctness_anchor: Lowering the access barrier should preserve the intellectual goal.
application_anchor: Provide templates, pre-cut safe materials or partner support and gradually fade support.
reject_endorsement: Removing all student decisions or requiring unpracticed tool use.

correctness_anchor: A simple process assessment can follow planning, evidence and revision.
application_anchor: Give a three-part checklist with one concrete observation per part and a feedback/retry opportunity.
reject_endorsement: Scoring only decoration or claiming a checklist proves long-term growth.

correctness_anchor: A child can retain agency while receiving a smaller cutting task and a model.
application_anchor: Offer a visible guide and short supported attempt with suitable scissors and supervision, then fade help.
reject_endorsement: Completing the entire craft for the pupil or withholding help regardless of distress.

correctness_anchor: Troubleshooting a low-voltage circuit should isolate one possible fault at a time.
application_anchor: Ask the pupil to trace the closed path, inspect contacts and test one component, escalating hints only when needed.
reject_endorsement: Rewiring everything for the pupil or allowing short circuits.

correctness_anchor: A collapsed paper bridge provides evidence about the design, not the child's ability.
application_anchor: Acknowledge frustration, compare one structural change and retest under the same load conditions.
reject_endorsement: Praising an untested improvement as definitely stronger or labelling the child incapable.

correctness_anchor: Measurement requires a straight aligned scale, a correct starting mark and consistent endpoint reading.
application_anchor: Prompt the child to compare alignments and choose a stabilizing method, then repeat a measurement.
reject_endorsement: Giving a memorized length without correcting the measurement process.

correctness_anchor: A simple filter can reduce suspended particles but does not guarantee safe drinking water.
application_anchor: Guide one comparison of flow or layer arrangement and observe clarity without tasting the water.
reject_endorsement: Claiming clear filtered water is potable.

correctness_anchor: Magnification needs appropriate object-lens-eye geometry and adjustment.
application_anchor: Calmly model changing one distance and ask the pupil to find the clearest view using a leaf away from direct sun.
reject_endorsement: Looking at the sun or treating one fixed distance as universally correct.

correctness_anchor: A veering model car can have alignment, friction or thrust asymmetry.
application_anchor: Record the path, choose one hypothesis and change one factor before a new trial, with a pause if frustrated.
reject_endorsement: Claiming a specific cause without checking or changing every part simultaneously.

correctness_anchor: A specimen label needs legible identifying information linked to the right object.
application_anchor: Give a model with specimen ID, known name or unknown label, location and date, then a self-check.
reject_endorsement: Inventing a rock identification or collection site.

correctness_anchor: Simplification should preserve the central design idea while reducing construction demands.
application_anchor: Ask the pupil to choose one feature to retain, prototype a simpler structure and explain the tradeoff.
reject_endorsement: Dismissing the idea or taking over the whole design.

correctness_anchor: Overflow calls for a calm stop and teacher-managed cleanup before further inquiry.
application_anchor: After safety is restored, compare smaller measured quantities in an open appropriate container and record the change.
reject_endorsement: Sealing the gas-producing vessel or treating panic as disobedience.

correctness_anchor: An objective should specify observable performance and evidence, not merely know.
application_anchor: Refine the bulb goal into a safe low-voltage connection plus an explanation of the closed path, and align a check.
reject_endorsement: Claiming components named from memory alone demonstrate a working circuit.

correctness_anchor: Reported recall is a starting point, not evidence of explaining mechanisms or transfer.
application_anchor: Check a new seed example, then extend to explaining how a feature supports dispersal with evidence.
reject_endorsement: Repeating only names or assuming the entire class needs no further learning.

correctness_anchor: The goal should match available prerequisites while preserving the important concept.
application_anchor: Shift the core assessment to observable state changes and evidence, using a simple model only if it aids explanation.
reject_endorsement: Treating an oversimplified molecular story as a directly observed fact.

correctness_anchor: Two classes can share a core objective while differing in scaffolds and extension.
application_anchor: State a common magnetism criterion and class-specific support/evidence routes based on the described needs.
reject_endorsement: Permanently lowering expectations for an entire labelled class.

correctness_anchor: Use the supplied requirement as a premise, not a verified quotation from an unavailable standard.
application_anchor: Deepen observation, comparison and evidence-based description without inventing extra compulsory content.
reject_endorsement: Claiming the official standard was checked or filling time with unrelated advanced facts.

correctness_anchor: Engineering objectives include justified design choices, testing and revision, not just producing an object.
application_anchor: Add a measurable temperature comparison under stated conditions and evidence for one revision with supervised use.
reject_endorsement: Guaranteeing a target temperature under unspecified weather.

correctness_anchor: Remembering phase order alone does not demonstrate a model of Moon phases.
application_anchor: Use a light-source/Earth/Moon model with a viewpoint explanation and an accessible check.
reject_endorsement: Explaining ordinary lunar phases as Earth's shadow.

correctness_anchor: Review goals should target connections and application.
application_anchor: Ask students to classify and justify new examples using evidence, then address identified misconceptions.
reject_endorsement: Replacing all review with a teacher's list of definitions.

correctness_anchor: Use the stated vocabulary and experience needs, not family status as a proxy for ability.
application_anchor: Set an observable sound-vibration goal with concrete demonstration, language support and an individual check.
reject_endorsement: Assuming left-behind children cannot understand science.

correctness_anchor: The science objective should concern observable plant characteristics and evidence-based comparison.
application_anchor: Align diaries and drawings with accurate observation records and a science-specific criterion.
reject_endorsement: Grading artistic skill as the principal evidence of scientific learning.

correctness_anchor: Immediate grabbing calls for a calm pause and controlled access before further explanation.
application_anchor: Give a short stop cue, secure materials if needed, model one handling action and reopen access after a brief practice.
reject_endorsement: Continuing a long explanation while unsafe grabbing persists or humiliating the class.

correctness_anchor: Attention during instructions depends on material access and clear sequence.
application_anchor: Give a directly usable short cue and visible response, demonstrate it, rehearse once and check pupils who did not respond.
reject_endorsement: Shouting over ongoing unsafe activity or punishing every distracted pupil.

correctness_anchor: Work-time variation needs essential checkpoints and useful extensions.
application_anchor: Give a visible timebox, check a stalled group and offer finishers an evidence-based extension.
reject_endorsement: Assuming every slow pupil is deliberately wasting time.

correctness_anchor: Distribution should use designated roles and a rehearsed handover.
application_anchor: Prepare small sets, call one materials person per group and stop pushing before continuing.
reject_endorsement: Distributing materials into a scramble or using collective humiliation.

correctness_anchor: A stop cue must be understood and practiced, with accessible forms.
application_anchor: Rehearse a brief stop-and-hands-clear action, check who missed it and reteach accordingly.
reject_endorsement: Treating a conditioned response as automatic or imposing escalating punishment without checking access.

correctness_anchor: Consistency can reduce confusion when teachers agree on meanings.
application_anchor: Confirm the existing cue, retain its action and explain any science-specific addition.
reject_endorsement: Using the same cue for contradictory actions.

correctness_anchor: Young children can learn rules through concrete modeling and practice.
application_anchor: Act out a correct and safely simulated incorrect handover, then let pupils demonstrate the expected action.
reject_endorsement: Demonstrating an actually dangerous act to make the point.

correctness_anchor: A temporary material pause can address immediate risk while retaining a route back to participation.
application_anchor: Explain the specific behavior, reteach and allow a supported retry after the situation is safe.
reject_endorsement: Permanent exclusion or confiscation as humiliation.

correctness_anchor: The end of a lesson needs safe closure and a minimum evidence checkpoint.
application_anchor: Stop in time to store materials, record current observations and plan continuation where feasible.
reject_endorsement: Keeping hazardous work running past supervision or declaring unfinished work worthless.

correctness_anchor: Different classroom behavior needs investigation of routines and task demands.
application_anchor: Observe transitions, coordinate cues with the homeroom teacher and test one change before generalizing.
reject_endorsement: Concluding the science teacher or pupils are inherently incapable.

correctness_anchor: Magnets do not attract all metals or all materials.
application_anchor: Sequence predictions, observations on named materials, explanation and a transfer question with contingent follow-ups.
reject_endorsement: Teaching that every metal is magnetic.

correctness_anchor: A correct statement can be opened for evidence and peer reasoning.
application_anchor: Ask classmates to identify the observed evidence, compare an alternative explanation and extend the answer respectfully.
reject_endorsement: Only saying correct or requiring peers to repeat the same sentence.

correctness_anchor: Leaf observations can be organized by a shared dimension without erasing varied observations.
application_anchor: Focus on one feature, compare two examples and then broaden with a reasoned question.
reject_endorsement: Treating all unexpected observations as wrong.

correctness_anchor: Silence may reflect preparation or participation barriers.
application_anchor: Give thinking/pair time, ask for one observation or question about the report and invite a low-pressure response.
reject_endorsement: Forcing immediate public answers or assuming no learning occurred.

correctness_anchor: A controlled pendulum comparison changes one variable while keeping effective length and release amplitude appropriate.
application_anchor: Progress from what changed to what stayed fixed, repeated timing and an evidence-based conclusion.
reject_endorsement: Inferring mass causes period change from an uncontrolled trial.

correctness_anchor: Engineering questions can ask about criteria, tradeoffs and evidence from testing.
application_anchor: Ask students to predict how a lens-position change affects the image, test it and justify a revision.
reject_endorsement: Equating assembly completion with understanding or directing viewing of the sun.

correctness_anchor: Different participation patterns need varied response routes but a shared scientific goal.
application_anchor: Use the same sound-vibration question with quiet thinking/writing or exploratory extensions and check understanding in both classes.
reject_endorsement: Assuming talkativeness measures scientific ability.

correctness_anchor: An incorrect answer is evidence for a follow-up, not a reason for personal criticism.
application_anchor: Ask for reasoning, supply a counterexample or observation and invite a revised explanation.
reject_endorsement: Endorsing the incorrect science to protect feelings or publicly humiliating the student.

correctness_anchor: Physical versus chemical change concerns whether new substances form, not reversibility alone.
application_anchor: Compare evidence in a new example and ask what additional observation would support a claim.
reject_endorsement: Using irreversible as a sufficient definition of chemical change.

correctness_anchor: Unexpected answers should be checked for relevance and underlying reasoning.
application_anchor: Follow one productive idea with evidence questions, correct misconceptions and return to the core objective when needed.
reject_endorsement: Forcing every answer back to the guide's exact wording.

correctness_anchor: A quick role conflict needs a fair temporary procedure and a later turn for each pupil.
application_anchor: Use a brief rotation or agreed selection, model role duties and resume with a check.
reject_endorsement: Automatically failing any temporary teacher assignment or allowing one permanent leader.

correctness_anchor: Reluctance to lead may reflect unclear duties or pressure.
application_anchor: Clarify a small supported leader task, offer co-leading or a temporary scaffold and rotate later.
reject_endorsement: Forcing one unwilling pupil into public leadership without support.

correctness_anchor: Monopolizing equipment requires an immediate clear boundary with respectful feedback.
application_anchor: Pause the handover, specify turns and give the pupil a constructive role while verifying others' access.
reject_endorsement: Avoiding all intervention to prevent public criticism or labelling the pupil as bad.

correctness_anchor: A quiet pupil needs a meaningful accessible choice, not a permanent peripheral role.
application_anchor: Offer a prepared or partner-supported contribution and check privately what helps.
reject_endorsement: Always assigning quiet children to recording or forcing a public performance.

correctness_anchor: Turn-taking is learned through a visible simple sequence.
application_anchor: Model passing an object, rehearse short turns and use a visual cue with feedback.
reject_endorsement: Explaining only abstract fairness to first-graders.

correctness_anchor: Agreed random selection can be one tool when roles are safe and equitable over time.
application_anchor: Combine it with clear duties, rotation and teacher intervention if exclusion or access barriers appear.
reject_endorsement: Treating any student vote or lottery as automatically fair.

correctness_anchor: Exclusion needs teacher action based on observed behavior and a protected route to participation.
application_anchor: Check the situation, stop exclusion, assign a meaningful supported contribution and follow up privately.
reject_endorsement: Leaving the targeted student without a role to preserve group autonomy.

correctness_anchor: A pupil with weaker practical skills needs scaffolded access to real work.
application_anchor: Choose a manageable operation, model or partner-support it and recognize observed progress.
reject_endorsement: Permanently excluding the pupil from operation or fabricating success.

correctness_anchor: Roles should divide real work and rotate, with workload checked.
application_anchor: Define concrete responsibilities and one handover rule, then check every member's contribution.
reject_endorsement: Fixed personality-based roles that make some children permanent bystanders.

correctness_anchor: Teacher-assigned roles can be a temporary scaffold that is gradually reduced.
application_anchor: Move from modeled assignment to guided rotation and student negotiation with review criteria.
reject_endorsement: Claiming all direct assignment is inherently prohibited.

correctness_anchor: A sinking paper clip is an observation, not a failed student. Surface support depends on placement, surface condition and wetting; flotation is not guaranteed.
application_anchor: Say what was observed, invite one testable explanation, and compare gentle placement in clean water with the original attempt.
reject_endorsement: Promising every paper clip floats or replacing observations with the textbook result.

correctness_anchor: Immobile earthworms do not establish a moisture preference. Acclimation, lighting, temperature and moisture can affect behavior.
application_anchor: Allow observation time, compare conditions while changing one factor and protect the organisms; record no movement honestly.
reject_endorsement: Forcing movement, drying organisms deliberately or interpreting immobility as a clear choice.

correctness_anchor: Check whether the facing ends really are like poles and whether both objects are magnets before revising the claim about poles.
application_anchor: Label ends consistently and use a known magnet to check the pole identification, then repeat and document.
reject_endorsement: Declaring magnetism disproved or changing the recorded result to match a textbook.

correctness_anchor: Failure to extinguish the candle does not identify a unique cause: gas quantity, mixing and delivery are hypotheses, not observed facts.
application_anchor: Acknowledge uncertainty, record setup and propose one controlled comparison; any flame demonstration is teacher-managed and gas is not trapped in a sealed vessel.
reject_endorsement: Inventing a certain cause or requiring children to reproduce flames at home.

correctness_anchor: One week without visible bending does not show that plants never respond to light. Directional light, growth and observation conditions need checking.
application_anchor: Compare documented light conditions and growth over time with otherwise similar plants; make a prediction before observing.
reject_endorsement: Guaranteeing a bend by a fixed date or dismissing the observation.

correctness_anchor: Touch may damp a tuning fork and weak vibration can be hard to feel. A teacher can state the scientific explanation while distinguishing it from the evidence students observed.
application_anchor: Pair the explanation with a visible vibration indicator or an appropriate demonstration and a short follow-up check.
reject_endorsement: Claiming an unfelt vibration disproves sound vibration, or banning all direct explanation.

correctness_anchor: For a small-amplitude ideal pendulum, T=2*pi*sqrt(L/g), independent of bob mass. Length runs from pivot to the center of mass.
application_anchor: Control effective length and release amplitude, time several oscillations and repeat before comparing masses; discuss measurement uncertainty.
reject_endorsement: Using bob mass as the ideal-period cause or altering measurements to match theory.

correctness_anchor: A bulb needs an intact closed low-voltage circuit connecting its two contacts to the source. Contacts, bulb and battery are separate possible faults.
application_anchor: Offer graduated checks of one component at a time, beginning with the complete path; use only classroom low-voltage equipment and avoid short circuits.
reject_endorsement: Inferring inability from failure or recommending mains electricity.

correctness_anchor: Rust rates depend on exposure and material conditions, including moisture, oxygen and coatings; identical rates are not guaranteed.
application_anchor: Compare the groups' condition records, identify confounds and agree on a controlled follow-up while retaining the different observations.
reject_endorsement: Discarding slow-rusting samples as wrong or assuming one universal rate.

correctness_anchor: A ketchup volcano is a model whose behavior depends on its stated mechanism; do not assume an unspecified acid-base reaction.
application_anchor: Assign a drawing, prediction and one safe unsealed model comparison with an adult where needed; distinguish the model from real magma.
reject_endorsement: Increasing pressure in a sealed container or equating ketchup flow with real volcanic mechanisms.

correctness_anchor: A missing alcohol lamp does not justify improvising an unsafe heat source.
application_anchor: Use a suitable supervised demonstration if equipment exists, otherwise a video plus safe observations and explicit limits on what was observed directly.
reject_endorsement: Requiring children to heat water unsupervised or rejecting every video alternative.

correctness_anchor: Different materials can distract from the target shape comparison.
